worked_solution:
For expressions involving subtraction, De Moivre's theorem states that

$$
{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]}^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=8$ and $\phi =6\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\theta )]^{8} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\cdot 6\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\cdot 6\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(48\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(48\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$
